title: China's coke makers are squeezed between costlier coal supplies and their customers’ falling steel prices
dek: Chinese coke makers face a margin squeeze from costlier coal and falling steel prices among their customers, according to ISI Markets.
summary: ISI Markets reports that China's coke makers are being squeezed between rising coal supply costs and falling steel prices at their customers. The publisher's excerpt does not give price levels, margins or volumes.
keyFacts: Coal supplies to Chinese coke makers have become costlier.
Steel prices at coke makers' customers are falling.
whyItMatters: A margin squeeze in the coking segment could prompt output cuts or price disputes along China's blast-furnace supply chain, which influences seaborne coking coal and coke trade.
implications: Readers should watch for coke production curbs or price negotiations between Chinese coke makers and steel mills, which could affect met coal demand and coke export availability.
